metaTitle: Pallet Calculators: Truckload, Boxes per Pallet, Weight, Cost per Trip — AGL Pallet
metaDescription: Free pallet planning calculators: pallets per truckload, boxes per pallet, wood pallet weight estimate, and cost per trip. Server-rendered results with stated methods and sources.

sections.heading: How these calculators work
paragraphs: Each calculator is a plain form. Enter your figures and submit; the page is recalculated on the server and the result comes back as HTML text and tables, so it can be read, printed, or copied without scripts.

Every calculator states its method, its default values, and where each default comes from. None of them holds AGL price data or measured AGL weights: defaults are published figures or clearly labeled examples, and the cost calculator uses only the figures you enter.

items.question: How many boxes fit on a pallet?
answer: Cartons per layer times the layers that fit under the height limit, for a column-stacked load with no overhang. The example preset is on [How many boxes fit on a pallet?](/resources/questions/how-many-boxes-fit-on-a-pallet/), and the [boxes per pallet calculator](/resources/pallet-calculators/boxes-per-pallet/) takes your own carton.

items.question: Are the calculator results exact?
answer: No. They are planning estimates built on the inputs and the stated method. Real loads change with pallet tolerances, equipment, loading patterns, moisture, and receiver rules. Use the results to plan, then confirm with your carrier, receiver, and supplier.

items.question: Is there a pallet price calculator?
answer: Not yet. AGL does not publish dollar price bands until they can be drawn from real quotes. The cost per trip calculator works from your own purchase price, and a quote on your spec gives a delivered price.
